paragraphs.text: A lightweight DeepSeek API Peak/Off-Peak indicator for DeepSeek Harness Desktop.
# DeepSeek Peak Indicator
**English** · فارسی · 简体中文

A lightweight DeepSeek Harness plugin that shows the **current DeepSeek API pricing period** —
Peak

or Off-Peak — directly in the sidebar footer, from application start, with no Session open.
Click it
to see the **countdown to the next pricing transition**.

It needs no API key, makes no network requests and does not poll anything: the schedule is
computed
locally from the clock and a bundled, verified Chinese holiday calendar.

> **Peak means the official API pricing period, not server congestion or server health.**
> The indi

cator reports the billing period defined by DeepSeek; it says nothing about API load,
> latency or a
vailability. Peak prices are the higher **peak** rate; Off-Peak is the half-price rate.
## Install

**Requires DeepSeek Harness Desktop v0.2.1-rc.5 or later.** The plugin's runtime behavior is
unchang
ed. No extra runtime, build step or npm dependency is needed.

The package is `@jalilahmad.fazeli/deepseek-peak-indicator`. Install it from npm or directly from

## Features

- **One glance, three states** — 🟢 `OFF-PEAK`, 🔴 `PEAK`, ⚪ `UNKNOWN`.
- **Next-transition countdown*

* — the popover shows the remaining time in whole hours and minutes.
- **Accurate boundaries** — the

status flips exactly at the official period boundary; the countdown
refreshes once a minute and an

exact timer handles the transition itself.
- **Always present** — a root-scoped sidebar-footer entry

that exists before any Session,
Conversation or Composer is opened.
- **Holiday-aware** — verified

Chinese public-holiday dates for 2025 and 2026; an unverified year is
reported honestly as **UNKNOWN

**, never guessed.
- **Timezone-safe** — the schedule is evaluated in UTC, holiday dates in China St

andard Time, and all
conversions use the browser's IANA `Intl` database (no hardcoded offsets, DST-s

afe).
- **Tiny and private** — one client bundle, one Host row, one 60-second timer plus one transit

ion
timer; no API key, backend, database, telemetry or network polling.
- **Clean lifecycle** — time

rs, listeners, observers and styles are all disposed on unload; reloading
creates exactly one indica

listeners, observers and styles are all disposed on unload; reloading
creates exactly one indicator.
## How it works

The indicator registers in **`sidebar.footer.action`**, the root-scoped list slot beside Settings,
d

eclared by the shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar` package. It is part of the permanent
app

lication shell, so it does not depend on a Session, Conversation or Composer. The expanded
sidebar s
hows a small pill (dot + label); the 56 px rail shows the dot-only compact form.
## Privacy and architecture

- **No API key.** The plugin never asks for, stores or uses one.
- **No backend, no database, no sto

rage.** There is no server component and no account access.
- **No network requests, no polling, no

telemetry.** `client.js` contains no `fetch`,
`XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, `EventSource` or dynami

c `import()`; it reads the local clock and
the bundled holiday table only.
- **No secrets in the rep

ository.** No keys, tokens, personal paths or machine-specific state.
- **Standard plugin caveat.**

Like every DSH plugin, plugin code runs with the Harness application's
local permissions. Review the

source before installing; details and reporting are in
SECURITY.md.
The plugin is a DSH bundle with an empty Host half and a browser-side Client half:

1. `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` (the Cordis patch that inserts the Loader row) and
`dsh.clie

nt` (the browser entry).
2. `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the plugin row; `index.js` is a deliberately

empty `apply()`.
3. `client.js` registers a lazy module factory, adds the locale dictionaries, and r

egisters the
indicator in `sidebar.footer.action` through `ctx.slots`.
4. One wall-clock state, one

60-second interval and one exact transition timer drive the UI; all of
them are cleaned up when the

and one exact transition timer drive the UI; all of
them are cleaned up when the slot entry unloads.

The complete design, status algorithm, transition search and cleanup rules are in
`docs/architecture

omplete design, status algorithm, transition search and cleanup rules are in
`docs/architecture.md`.
## Compatibility and limitations
- **Verified on DeepSeek Harness Desktop v0.2.1-rc.5 (Windows).** `engines.dsh` allows this version

and all later DSH versions, including prereleases; later versions are not verified here and may
intr

oduce breaking changes. Other clients and platforms are not claimed compatible.
- **Windows collapse

d sidebar.** On the Windows titlebar layout the shipped sidebar shell hides its
entire footer when t

he sidebar is collapsed (including the shipped Settings control), so the
indicator is visible in the

default expanded sidebar but not in that collapsed state. The
dot-only compact form is used in the

56 px rail where the shell renders the footer.
- **2027 holiday data.** 2027 weekday peak windows sh

ow **UNKNOWN** until the official notice is
published and the calendar is updated. Weekends and off-

hours remain certain.
- **Package identity.** The public package is `@jalilahmad.fazeli/deepseek-pea

k-indicator`; this is
also the Harness module/package identity used by both npm and GitHub installs.

Installations made
before this rename (under `@local/deepseek-peak-indicator`) should be removed fi

rst and then
reinstalled. The plugin row id `deepseek-peak-indicator` and all runtime behavior are u

nchanged.
- **Screenshots.** Three real captures are shipped; PEAK and UNKNOWN captures require genu

ine
schedule conditions and remain pending. See
Screenshots and SCREENSHOTS_NEEDED.md.
